title: Painful Red Eye: Acute Glaucoma Versus Uveitis
subject: Ophthalmology
preview: Acute angle-closure glaucoma may cause severe eye pain, headache, halos, nausea and a hazy cornea.
quickRevision: Acute angle-closure glaucoma may cause severe eye pain, headache, halos, nausea and a hazy cornea.
A painful red eye with visual loss demands urgent ocular assessment.
Pupil response, corneal appearance, intraocular pressure when safe and anterior chamber findings help differentiation.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Acute angle-closure glaucoma may cause severe eye pain, headache, halos, nausea and a hazy cornea.
Anterior uveitis can cause photophobia and a constricted pupil; slit-lamp assessment is important.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: A painful red eye with visual loss demands urgent ocular assessment.
Pupil response, corneal appearance, intraocular pressure when safe and anterior chamber findings help differentiation.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not prescribe steroid eye drops empirically before excluding sight-threatening conditions.
